stem.en: Could a thin membrane alone protect a cell in every environment?

text.en: Yes, biological membranes are completely indestructible.

feedback.en: Biological membranes are not indestructible. They can be damaged by physical forces, drying, or changes in their surroundings. Many cells therefore need additional protection.

text.en: No, extreme environments require additional rigid structures like cell walls.
Yes, but only if the cell constantly pumps water out.

feedback.en: Constantly pumping water out would require a great deal of energy and would not protect the membrane from physical damage. A rigid cell wall provides a much more effective solution.

explanation.en: A thin membrane is flexible and excellent for controlling what enters and leaves the cell, but it is not strong enough to withstand every environment. Many organisms evolved a cell wall, which provides additional mechanical support and protection while still allowing the membrane to perform its selective transport role.
